---
title: "A beginner handoff with a different simulation bank"
---

First run the [quickstart](quickstart.qmd). Then practice the full handoff on a
small synthetic stock/flux bank, independent of the bundled SIRDS example.
This checks data handling and software use; its short training run makes no
scientific accuracy claim and is not an agent-based simulation benchmark.

## Practice with a CSV

Save [own_bank.py](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/examples/own_bank.py)
as `own_bank.py` in your uv project. It generates 30 parameter settings, three
replicates and 12 timepoints, with static inputs `decay` and `forcing` and
outputs `stock` and `flux`. The toy recurrence and its noise are explicit in
the script. No SIRDS or malaria bank is trained by this exercise.

```bash
uv run python own_bank.py --make-bank-only
uv run metis inspect-data own-bank/bank.parquet --inputs decay forcing --outputs stock flux
uv run python own_bank.py --csv own-bank/bank.csv --steps 100
```

The first command writes CSV and Parquet. The second validates the bank without
training. The final command loads the CSV with Polars, validates it through
`SimulationDataset.from_frame`, splits by input group, fits an MLP, evaluates
held-out groups, and saves `model.pt`, `evaluation.json` and `prediction.npy`
inside `own-bank/`. Inspect the per-output errors; successful execution alone
does not establish that the fit is useful.

Run this in a fresh Python process to check deployment:

```python
from metis import Surrogate
model = Surrogate.load("own-bank/model.pt")
print(model.predict({"decay": 0.2, "forcing": 0.6}).shape)  # (1, 12, 2)
```

Save it as `predict.py` and use `uv run python predict.py`. This process does
not read the original bank.

## Substitute your real bank

Aggregate your agent records into trajectories first. Replace the script's
explicit `INPUTS`/`OUTPUTS` lists with your column names; do not merely rename
unrelated quantities. Choose consistent time and replicate identifiers, units,
parameter groups and scientific outputs. The exercise's later standalone
prediction snippet also needs your own parameter names and values. For an existing CSV the central step is:

```python
import polars as pl
from metis import SimulationDataset
frame = pl.read_csv("my_bank.csv")
bank = SimulationDataset.from_frame(
    frame, inputs=["contact_rate", "recovery_rate"],
    outputs=["incidence", "prevalence"],
)
```

Use the [data contract](data.qmd) to resolve errors. Preserve test groups while
you tune on validation. Decide your acceptable error in original units and any
scientific constraints before interpreting a fit. A new grid, partially observed
records or categorical inputs requires an explicit preparation decision.

## What is checked automatically

The repository's `scripts/check_beginner_handoff.py` creates a new uv project,
installs a built wheel, runs this CSV exercise and validates a fresh-process
reload. It also runs the installed Hydra transformer with an observed channel,
saves a training checkpoint and checks compatible resume and artifact parity. It is an automated acceptance check, **not an observed human usability
trial**. A real new starter should also be asked to explain the input schema,
held-out result and limits of their predictions; those scientific explanations
cannot be inferred from a passing script.
